caption: The drawing depicts a stylized rooster composed almost entirely of reddish-brown tones. The rooster's body, wings, and tail feathers are depicted with segmented and textured sections that suggest metallic or carved construction, with rivets or bolts visible on several of the pieces, especially on the tail feathers and wing plates. The comb, wattles, and beak are also colored in reddish and ochre hues, with the beak appearing lighter, almost yellowish at the tip. The eyes are detailed with a blue center and surrounding shapes, giving a layered effect. The legs and feet are depicted in a pale, beige color and appear jointed. The rooster stands with both legs extended and is supported by a vertical rod that is inserted between its legs, suggesting it may be a model or weathervane. The background is plain and pale, with no additional objects or scenery.
title: Weather Vane
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
